{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-sc-d","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"ee9823b97a45305908f915bec3c92584ba3dffe21b1d2c1de136e7358d2ab89d","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-sc-class-d:lineage:55","source_registry_sha256":"61c32f86a25e3c021742b3c9ddf64a97709817dd75a19df6d2b69eac0a40c4f1","source_liveness_sha256":"feb7871590284d2a19ab0509ff65b48154ba15e637a6ec9b839f55a72736ffdb"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C2"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C2","chunk_id":"C2.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Pedestrian, bicycle, motorcycle and truck confusables","heading":"C2 — Continuation facts, then confusable pairs and knowledge-graph hints: ready-to-yield versus must-yield, yielding versus a full stop, skillful versus unskillful cyclists, motorcycle spacing and truck blind spots","learner_facing":false,"markdown":"## C2 — Continuation facts, then confusable pairs and knowledge-graph hints: ready-to-yield versus must-yield, yielding versus a full stop, skillful versus unskillful cyclists, motorcycle spacing and truck blind spots
Continuation facts on courtesy, pedestrians, bicyclists, mopeds and trucks, plus confusable pairs among the road-sharing duties; each block ties to one handbook page, and hint metadata sits only in the trailing line of a block.

FACT_ID: sec13-R01 | anchor: A01
Be courteous and let other road users know where you are and what you plan to do, which helps avoid collisions. [A01]
Why it matters: group courtesy; difficulty low.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0109]

FACT_ID: sec13-R02 | anchor: A01
Pedestrians are hard to see, and it is hard to tell what they intend to do. [A01]
Why it matters: group pedestrians; difficulty low.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0109]

FACT_ID: sec13-R03 | anchor: A01
Outside a crosswalk you must be prepared to yield to pedestrians, while inside any crosswalk, marked or not, you are required to yield. [A01]
Why it matters: group pedestrians; confusable be prepared to yield versus must yield.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0109]

FACT_ID: sec13-R04 | anchor: A01
For most pedestrians the duty is to yield, but a pedestrian crossing with a guide dog or a white cane requires a complete stop. [A01]
Why it matters: group pedestrians; confusable yield versus complete stop.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0109]

FACT_ID: sec13-R05 | anchor: A02
The school zone speed limit applies either when its lights are flashing or when children are present, not only when both are true. [A02]
Why it matters: group school zones; difficulty medium.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0110]

FACT_ID: sec13-R06 | anchor: A03
Bicyclists may not be easy to spot in traffic, so stay alert and take extra care when approaching them. [A03]
Why it matters: group bicyclists; difficulty low.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0111]

FACT_ID: sec13-R07 | anchor: A03
Like drivers, bicyclists have different skill levels, and the unskillful rider is the one to expect sudden swerves from. [A03]
Why it matters: group bicyclists; confusable skillful versus unskillful rider.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0111]

FACT_ID: sec13-R08 | anchor: A03
The horn near a bicyclist is reserved for a real chance of collision, not for simply announcing that you are there. [A03]
Why it matters: group bicyclists; confusable warning versus announcing presence.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0111]

FACT_ID: sec13-R09 | anchor: A05
Check for bicyclists in your path before backing up, especially near schools and in residential areas where they are more likely. [A05]
Why it matters: group bicyclists; difficulty low.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0113]

FACT_ID: sec13-R10 | anchor: A07
Scooters and mopeds travel much more slowly than motorcycles. [A07]
Why it matters: group motorcycles; confusable moped versus motorcycle speed.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0115]

FACT_ID: sec13-R11 | anchor: A07
The four-second gap behind a motorcycle is a minimum, and wet conditions call for more. [A07]
Why it matters: group motorcycles; difficulty medium.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0115]

FACT_ID: sec13-R12 | anchor: A08
A truck's blind spot is larger on its right side than its left, starting behind the cab and reaching up to the truck's length. [A08]
Why it matters: group trucks; confusable right side versus left side.
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0116]

FACT_ID: sec13-R13 | anchor: A08
No zones exist at the front and rear of large trucks and buses as well as on their sides. [A08]
Why it matters: group trucks; difficulty low.
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0116]
